• **Lord Dalhousie** served as **Viceroy of India** from **1848 to 1856 **and was known for his** policy of annexation**, which led to the annexation of several **princely states** in India.
 
• **Lord Curzon** served as** Viceroy of India** from **1899 to 1905** and was known for his **administrative reforms,** including the** partition of Bengal** in **1905**, which was later revoked due to protests.
 
• Hence, the **correct answer **is option **3**, Lord Louis Mountbatten.

questions.question: Who was the Viceroy of India when Mahatma Gandhi started Dandi March on 12 March 1930?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Irwin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lord Irwin served as the Viceroy of India from 1926 to 1931.
 
• During his tenure, Mahatma Gandhi launched the Salt March, also known as the Dandi March, on 12 March 1930.
 
• The Dandi March was a pivotal event in the Indian independence movement, protesting against the British salt monopoly.
 
• Lord Irwin was known for his efforts to engage with Indian leaders, leading to the historic Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 1931.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dandi March:**

 
 
• The Dandi March, also known as the Salt March, was a 24-day, 240-mile (390 km) march led by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• It began on 12 March 1930 and ended on 5 April 1930.
 
• It was a direct action campaign of tax resistance and nonviolent protest against the British salt monopoly.
 
• The march was a significant event in the Indian independence movement, garnering worldwide attention and inspiring numerous Indians to join the struggle for independence.
 
 
 
• **Gandhi-Irwin Pact:**
 
 
• Signed on 5 March 1931 between Mahatma Gandhi and Lord Irwin, the then Viceroy of India.
 
• The pact marked the end of the civil disobedience movement in India.
 
• As part of the agreement, the British agreed to release all political prisoners, and Gandhi agreed to discontinue the Salt Satyagraha.
 
• The pact paved the way for Gandhi to attend the Round Table Conference in London to discuss India's future constitutional status.
 
 
 
• **Lord Irwin:**
 
 
• Lord Irwin, later known as Lord Halifax, was the Viceroy of India from 1926 to 1931.
 
• His tenure was marked by significant events like the Simon Commission, the Nehru Report, and the Salt March.
 
• He played a crucial role in negotiations with Indian leaders and was instrumental in the signing of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
 
• Lord Irwin's tenure is often remembered for his attempts to reconcile British interests with Indian aspirations for self-governance.

questions.question: Under whom among the following British Governor -Generals was the new policy of ‘paramountcy’ initiated in British India by the East India Company?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The new policy of **'paramountcy'** was initiated in British India by the East India Company under the British Governor-General **Lord Hastings**.
 
• Lord Hastings served as the Governor-General of India from **1813 to 1823**.
 
• The policy of paramountcy aimed to establish the supremacy of the British East India Company over the Indian states.
 
• It marked a shift from the earlier policy of non-interference to one of active intervention in the affairs of Indian princely states.
 
• This policy laid the foundation for the eventual establishment of British paramountcy over the entire Indian subcontinent.

• Lord Hastings' real name was **Francis Rawdon-Hastings**, and he was the 1st Marquess of Hastings.
 
• He played a crucial role in the **Third Anglo-Maratha War** (1817-1818), which resulted in the defeat of the Maratha Empire and the expansion of British control in India.
 
• His tenure also saw the implementation of various administrative and military reforms that strengthened British rule in India.
 
• The policy of paramountcy was later continued and expanded by subsequent British Governor-Generals.
